Source: [plugins/kubernetes/doc.go](https://github.com/agentshield-dev/agentshield/blob/main/plugins/kubernetes/doc.go).

Package kubernetes is the Kubernetes source plugin and the shared Kubernetes observation layer that the Istio, agentgateway, and Cilium plugins build on.

<span id="hdr-Watches_and_collections"></span>

## Watches and collections

The plugin owns API discovery and one dynamic shared informer factory per cluster. It always watches a required core inventory (namespaces, nodes, pods, services, workloads, RBAC, admission, NetworkPolicy, Ingress, and related resources) and the optional gateway-api-v1 capability. Semantic plugins add GroupVersionResources through [ResourceRequirementsProvider](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/agentshield-dev/agentshield/plugins/kubernetes#ResourceRequirementsProvider); the host merges them with [ResourceRequirements](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/agentshield-dev/agentshield/plugins/kubernetes#ResourceRequirements) before construction, so each GVR is watched once no matter how many plugins need it. Every watched GVR is published as its own kubernetes/resources/\<group>/\<version>/\<resource> collection, and [CollectionResourceCoverage](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/agentshield-dev/agentshield/plugins/kubernetes#CollectionResourceCoverage) reports per-capability API coverage. Consumers read these through [ResourceClient](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/agentshield-dev/agentshield/plugins/kubernetes#ResourceClient) rather than opening their own watches.

Secret observations carry metadata and a sorted key list only; values, type, and annotations never enter a collection or the native-event store.

<span id="hdr-Identity"></span>

## Identity

Kubernetes objects use the kubernetes.io/v1 Object scheme with the configured cluster ID as authority and the lowercased apiVersion/kind/UID as the immutable key (see [ClaimFor](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/agentshield-dev/agentshield/plugins/kubernetes#ClaimFor) and [ClaimForUID](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/agentshield-dev/agentshield/plugins/kubernetes#ClaimForUID)). Names, labels, and IP addresses are attributes. Every plugin asserting about a Kubernetes object reuses this scheme so its claims converge on the same graph resource. Service and Pod addresses materialize provider-neutral network destinations under the configured network ID, with exposes edges from their owners.

<span id="hdr-Graph_output"></span>

## Graph output

The "inventory" contribution asserts resources plus contains, runs-on, instantiates, uses-identity, exposes, member-of, governed-by, and backed-by relationships and network-exposure, transport-posture, policy-targeting, and route-backends facets. Node-to-cloud-instance backed-by edges are emitted only when a configured IdentityReferenceResolver (for example the AWS plugin) resolves the Node's spec.providerID.

<span id="hdr-Failure_behavior"></span>

## Failure behavior

An unavailable required API fails startup. An optional API that is not advertised is unsupported coverage; one that cannot be read is degraded and marks the contribution degraded. Neither proves the absence of unobserved objects. Each change replaces the complete contribution at the next generation; deletion is omission.

The package also implements the network-policy/v1 remediation action, which isolates a Pod's ingress with a NetworkPolicy and a controlled Pod label.

See docs/plugins/kubernetes.md and, for the plugin contract, docs/plugins/README.md.
